One-step actor-critic

Put Lessons 75 and 76 together. After every step, the critic computes the TD error $\delta$, learns from it like TD(0), and hands the same $\delta$ to the actor as an estimate of the advantage. Nobody waits for the episode to end.

Learning the slippery corridor

Each cell shows the actor's $\pi(\rightarrow \mid s)$ (green share of the bar) and the critic's $\hat v(s)$. Both start from zero: a coin-flip policy and a critic that expects nothing. $-1$ per step, 20% slip, $\gamma = 1$.

Actor-critic: $\alpha^{\boldsymbol\theta} = \alpha^{\mathbf w} = 0.2$. The maths

The actor is a policy $\pi(a \mid s, \boldsymbol\theta)$ and the critic a value estimate $\hat v(s, \mathbf w)$. Both update from the one-step TD error:

$$\delta_t = R_{t+1} + \gamma\, \hat v(S_{t+1}, \mathbf w) - \hat v(S_t, \mathbf w)$$

with $\hat v = 0$ at a terminal state. The critic does semi-gradient TD(0) (Lessons 45 and 62). The actor takes Lesson 76's advantage form of the policy gradient with $\delta_t$ standing in for $A_\pi(S_t, A_t)$ (S&B eq. 13.12):

$$\begin{aligned} \mathbf w &\leftarrow \mathbf w + \alpha^{\mathbf w}\, \delta_t\, \nabla \hat v(S_t, \mathbf w) \\ \boldsymbol\theta &\leftarrow \boldsymbol\theta + \alpha^{\boldsymbol\theta}\, \gamma^t\, \delta_t\, \nabla \ln \pi(A_t \mid S_t, \boldsymbol\theta) \end{aligned}$$

The critic moves its estimate towards the one-step target. The actor makes the action just taken more likely if it beat the critic's expectation, less likely if not.

One-step actor-critic (episodic, S&B §13.5)

Loop for each episode:

Initialise $S$ (first state); $I \leftarrow 1$

Loop while $S$ is not terminal:

$A \sim \pi(\cdot \mid S, \boldsymbol\theta)$; take $A$, observe $S', R$

$\delta \leftarrow R + \gamma\, \hat v(S', \mathbf w) - \hat v(S, \mathbf w)$

$\mathbf w \leftarrow \mathbf w + \alpha^{\mathbf w}\, \delta\, \nabla \hat v(S, \mathbf w)$

$\boldsymbol\theta \leftarrow \boldsymbol\theta + \alpha^{\boldsymbol\theta}\, I\, \delta\, \nabla \ln \pi(A \mid S, \boldsymbol\theta)$

$I \leftarrow \gamma I$; $\ S \leftarrow S'$

$I$ holds $\gamma^t$. In the corridor $\gamma = 1$, so $I = 1$ throughout.

Tabular case. With one value $\hat v(s)$ per cell, $\nabla \hat v(S)$ is 1 for cell $S$ and 0 elsewhere. With a softmax over preferences $h(s, b)$, eq. 13.9 gives $\partial \ln \pi(A \mid S) / \partial h(S, b) = \mathbb{1}_{b = A} - \pi(b \mid S)$. So each step changes

$$\begin{aligned} \hat v(S) &\leftarrow \hat v(S) + \alpha^{\mathbf w}\, \delta \\ h(S, A) &\leftarrow h(S, A) + \alpha^{\boldsymbol\theta}\, \delta\, \big(1 - \pi(A \mid S)\big) \\ h(S, b) &\leftarrow h(S, b) - \alpha^{\boldsymbol\theta}\, \delta\, \pi(b \mid S) \quad (b \ne A) \end{aligned}$$

These are the three lines printed under the corridor at every step.
